actual: AssertionError at tests/test_core_contracts.py:241 on the publish assertion topic_publishes(mqtt_mock, topic) == [] with the EAGER_TASK_HINT message: core MQTT published three retained None clears on the shared core-prefix discovery topic, assert [(None, True), (None, True), (None, True)] == []; every premise assertion before it held (one takeover-path call with UNKNOWN content and three loaded, enabled rows)
semanticAssessment: The target executed (1 test, 1 failure, 0 errors) and failed on the planned publish assertion with its own EAGER_TASK_HINT message. The RED came from the named temporary mutant in custom_components/mqtt_actions/takeover.py: in _remove_planned, the disable-first step (entity_registry.async_update_entity(..., disabled_by=INTEGRATION)) of an enabled row was replaced by pass, so the row is removed while its entity is still loaded and subscribed. Core MQTT then publishes its clear-on-remove for each of the three loaded rows (three retained None payloads on the shared topic). That is the same observable effect as a Home Assistant core without the eager task in Entity._async_registry_updated: there the disable would not unsubscribe the entity before the remove event, and the removal would again reach a loaded entity. Every premise assertion held under the mutant (the takeover-path call with UNKNOWN content saw three loaded, enabled rows), so the test failed for the intended reason. No import, collection or fixture fault. The mutant was reverted with git checkout before the commit and git diff --quiet -- custom_components/ was clean.
